subtitle: How a quiet village stone carried the first firm breath of written Kannada

panels.shot: low-angle close-up of a weathered stone pillar against a dusky sky, faint Kannada letters catching the light
panels.action: Halmidi Scribe stands beside an ancient inscribed stone in a quiet village field, his hand hovering near the carved letters as the evening sun carves long shadows.

dialogue.text: In a small field near Halmidi, a single stone bears one of the earliest clear voices of Kannada power, and the age of kings and land grants presses its weight into every line.

i18n.hi: हालमीड़ी के पास एक छोटे खेत में, एक पत्थर पर कन्नड़ शक्ति की शुरुआती गूँज है, जहाँ राजाओं और दानपत्रों का ज़ोर हर पंक्ति पर है।

panels.shot: slow push-in from aerial view of the Western Ghats into the forests around Banavasi and Halmidi
panels.action: From high above, thick green forests and winding rivers of early Karnataka stretch out as tiny clearings and hamlets like Halmidi nestle between fields and groves.

dialogue.text: Fifth-century Karnataka was a land of forests and red earth, where rivers fed paddy fields, and small villages owed their lives to kings they rarely saw.

i18n.hi: पाँचवीं सदी का कर्नाटक जंगलों, लाल मिट्टी और नदियों का देश था, जहाँ धान के खेतों और गाँवों की जान उन राजाओं पर थी जिन्हें उन्होंने शायद ही देखा।

panels.shot: wide shot of Banavasi town with wooden halls and a modest palace, villagers and officials moving about
panels.action: A modest but busy royal settlement at Banavasi shows timber-pillared halls, a shrine, and officials with palm-leaf bundles walking through the dusty streets.

dialogue.text: From Banavasi, the Kadambas ruled this world, their orders usually sung in Sanskrit and Prakrit, languages of priests, poets and imperial habit.

i18n.hi: बनवासी से कदंब राज करते थे, उनके हुक्म ज़्यादातर संस्कृत और प्राकृत में गाए जाते, पुरोहितों, कवियों और साम्राज्यों की ज़ुबान में।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a royal office, scribes seated with palm leaves, one older Brahmin scribe in focus
panels.action: Inside a shaded hall, an older Brahmin scribe bends over palm leaves, stylus poised, while another recites a Sanskrit formula; younger assistants listen carefully.

dialogue.text: Royal scribes were trained in these tongues; their formulas were old, their letters learned from distant dynasties, their habits bound to courts from Pataliputra to Kanchipuram.

i18n.hi: राजदरबार के लेखक इन्हीं भाषाओं में सधे थे; उनके फ़रमान पुराने, अक्षर दूर–दूर की राजधानियों से, आदतें पाटलिपुत्र से कांचीपुरम तक के दरबारों से बंधी।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Halmidi Scribe among other scribes, eyes thoughtful, fingers tracing a Kannada word on a scrap
panels.action: Halmidi Scribe, a younger official with a calm, sharp face, sits among the scribes, quietly tracing rounded Kannada letters on a palm scrap as others chant Sanskrit.

dialogue.text: Yet in their homes and villages, another tongue flowed—Kannada, a living speech of farmers and feudatories, already rich in song but still rare in stone.

i18n.hi: लेकिन घर–गाँव में एक और बोली बहती थी—कन्नड़, किसानों और सामंतों की ज़िंदा ज़ुबान, जो गीतों में समृद्ध थी पर पत्थर पर अभी कम।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a village discussion, local chiefs and a royal officer seated in a circle
panels.action: Under a large tree near Halmidi, a royal officer in fine cloth sits with local chiefs and elders, who gesture towards their fields and groves, faces earnest.

dialogue.text: Across villages like Halmidi, chiefs asked for grants, priests sought endowments, and kings sought loyalty; bargains were struck under trees before they were ever carved in rock.

i18n.hi: हालमीड़ी जैसे गाँवों में नायक दान माँगते, पुरोहित अनुदान, राजा निष्ठा; पेड़ों के नीचे सौदे होते, फिर कभी पत्थर पर उकेरे जाते।

panels.shot: medium shot of Halmidi Scribe standing by a stonecutter and a local chief, gesturing between a palm leaf and a blank stone pillar
panels.action: Halmidi Scribe stands with a local chief and a stonecutter before a blank stone pillar, one hand on a palm-leaf draft, the other indicating the empty surface.

dialogue.text: In one such moment, a decision was made: the grant would be set not just on palm leaves in the court, but on a stone in the village, where all could see.

i18n.hi: ऐसे ही एक वक्त फ़ैसला हुआ: दान सिर्फ़ दरबार की ताड़पत्र पर नहीं, गाँव के पत्थर पर भी लिखा जाएगा, ताकि सब देखें।

panels.shot: close-up on Halmidi Scribe’s face as he considers, faint anxiety and resolve in his eyes
panels.action: A close view shows Halmidi Scribe’s brow furrowed in thought, his gaze shifting from the villagers to the blank stone, sensing the weight of the choice before him.

dialogue.text: The script of power was ready in his hand, but the tongue of the people tugged at his ear; should the king’s will be voiced in their own Kannada words?

i18n.hi: उसके हाथ में सत्ता की लिपि थी, पर कानों में लोगों की बोली—क्या राजा की इच्छा उनकी अपनी कन्नड़ में दर्ज हो?

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of the scribe drafting on a palm leaf, lines in an early Kannada script taking shape
panels.action: From over his shoulder, we see Halmidi Scribe inscribing rounded early Kannada letters onto a palm leaf, carefully adapting known forms to fit familiar village words.

dialogue.text: Some letters had been used in Prakrit and Sanskrit records; now he bent them gently towards Kannada sounds, shaping a script that could carry his homeland’s speech.

i18n.hi: कुछ अक्षर पहले प्राकृत–संस्कृत में थे; उसने उन्हें हल्के से मोड़कर कन्नड़ ध्वनियों पर बैठाया, एक लिपि गढ़ी जो अपने देश की बोली ढो सके।

panels.shot: medium shot in a small shrine or court, scribe reading Kannada draft aloud to a senior official or priest
panels.action: Inside a small shrine-like hall, Halmidi Scribe reads his Kannada draft to a seated elder official, who listens, fingers resting on prayer beads, the draft between them.

dialogue.speaker: halmidi_inscription
dialogue.text: The land, the boundary, the curse—let them hear it in the tongue they know.

i18n.hi: ज़मीन, हद, शाप—सब उन्हें उसी ज़ुबान में सुनने दो जो वे जानते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a stonecutter carving the pillar while villagers watch, the scribe supervising
panels.action: Under open sky, a stonecutter chisels delicate early Kannada lines into the standing stone as Halmidi Scribe watches closely and villagers gather at a respectful distance.

dialogue.text: Line by line, a village bargain turned into an inscription, its phrases echoing traditional land-grant formulas, but now in a Kannada that farmers could follow.

i18n.hi: पंक्ति दर पंक्ति, गाँव का सौदा शिलालेख बना, वाक्य पुराने दान–सूत्र गूँजते रहे, पर अब ऐसे कन्नड़ में जिसे किसान पकड़ सकें।

panels.shot: tight close-up of the inscription’s lines, camera gliding along the carved letters
panels.action: A close, almost tactile view traces the rhythm of carved Kannada letters as they march across the stone, some uneven yet sure, shadows filling the grooves.

dialogue.text: This was no poem but a practical record: a land grant, a donor, a recipient, a king’s authority, a warning to violators—old structures now carried by a new written voice.

i18n.hi: ये कविता नहीं, काम की नोंद थी: ज़मीन का दान, दाता, प्राप्तकर्ता, राजा की मुहर, उल्लंघन करने वालों को चेतावनी—पुरानी ढाँचे, पर नई लिखित आवाज़ में।

panels.shot: medium shot of villagers gathered around the finished stone, an elder lightly touching the letters
panels.action: Villagers of different ages stand around the newly raised stone; an elder leans forward, fingertips hovering just above the fresh inscription with quiet awe.

dialogue.text: Around it, the village stirred; some could not read, but they knew this: their land, their gods, their king now met on a stone that spoke closer to their own tongue.

i18n.hi: चारों ओर गाँव हिला; कई पढ़ नहीं पाते थे, पर इतना समझ गए: उनकी ज़मीन, उनके देव, उनका राजा अब ऐसे पत्थर पर मिले जो उनकी बोली के क़रीब बोलता था।

panels.shot: soft-focus montage shot, fading between the Halmidi pillar, other imagined early Kannada grants, and palm-leaf records
panels.action: A blended scene shows the Halmidi pillar dissolving into glimpses of other early Kannada-inscribed stones and palm-leaf grants, hinting at a widening habit of Kannada record-keeping.

dialogue.text: Over time, such choices spread; Kannada crept further into charters and pillars, beside Sanskrit and Prakrit, joining the languages that carried law and lineage across the peninsula.

i18n.hi: धीरे–धीरे ऐसे फ़ैसले फैल गए; कन्नड़ भी फरमानों और स्तंभों पर चढ़ा, संस्कृत–प्राकृत के साथ, उन ज़ुबानों में जिसे कानून और वंशावली ढोती थी।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot showing the pillar weathering through sun, rain and overgrown fields across centuries
panels.action: The Halmidi stone stands as seasons whirl past in quick succession—rains darken it, creepers climb and retreat, nearby huts appear and vanish, yet the letters persist.

dialogue.text: Centuries turned; dynasties rose and fell; the pillar weathered in its field, its early Kannada script slowly softening but never falling entirely silent.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ मुड़ीं; वंश उठे–गिरे; स्तंभ खेत में ही घुलता रहा, उसकी शुरुआती कन्नड़ लिपि घिस गई, पर आवाज़ कभी पूरी खामोश न हुई।

panels.shot: medium shot of a 20th-century archaeologist in simple colonial-era attire studying the stone with notebook and tracing paper
panels.action: A modern-era archaeologist in the dress of the 1930s kneels beside the stone, pressing thin paper against the inscription and rubbing gently to take a copy, notebook open beside him.

dialogue.text: In the twentieth century, scholars like M.H. Krishna came searching; they copied, compared, and argued over scripts and sounds, calling Halmidi one of the earliest clear Kannada voices in stone.

i18n.hi: बीसवीं सदी में एम.एच. कृष्ण जैसे विद्वान पहुँचे; उन्होंने नकलें कीं, तुलना की, अक्षरों–ध्वनियों पर बहस की, और हालमीड़ी को पत्थर पर कन्नड़ की शुरुआती साफ़ आवाज़ों में गिना।

panels.shot: split composition: on one side, Halmidi stone; on the other, a fragment of the Talagunda lion balustrade in a lab
panels.action: The frame splits to show the Halmidi pillar on one side and, on the other, a carefully mounted lion-balustrade fragment from Talagunda in a modern lab, with Kannada-Sanskrit lines visible.

dialogue.text: Later finds like the Talagunda lion balustrade pushed back Kannada’s epigraphic past, reminding us that the story of firsts is always being revised by new stones and new readings.

i18n.hi: बाद में तलगुंड के सिंह–मंडप जैसे शिलालेख मिले, कन्नड़ लेखों को और पीछे धकेलते हुए, बताते कि ‘पहले’ की कहानियाँ नई खोजों से हमेशा बदलती रहती हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of a present-day Kannada reader’s hand on the Halmidi letters, with modern Kannada books visible in a bag
panels.action: A modern visitor’s hand rests gently on the ancient letters while a cloth bag at their side bulges with Kannada books, the old stone and the printed pages sharing the frame.

dialogue.text: Yet Halmidi holds a special weight, not as the single first word, but as a fully formed Kannada document where royal power, land, and language meet in a sharp, durable line.

i18n.hi: फिर भी हालमीड़ी की अपनी अहमियत है; पहला शब्द नहीं, पर पूरा कन्नड़ दस्तावेज, जहाँ राजसत्ता, ज़मीन और भाषा एक तेज़, टिकाऊ पंक्ति में मिलते हैं।

panels.shot: final wide shot at sunset, the Halmidi stone silhouetted against the sky, Halmidi Scribe’s figure imagined beside it
panels.action: At sunset, the Halmidi stone stands in silhouette on the field’s edge; faintly, as if from memory, the figure of Halmidi Scribe appears beside it, gaze turned towards the horizon.

dialogue.text: A language enters history when power learns to write it down; in Halmidi’s quiet field, Kannada stepped from speech and song into stone, and that step still shapes every word written today.

i18n.hi: भाषा इतिहास में तब उतरती है जब सत्ता उसे लिखना सीखती है; हालमीड़ी के शांत खेत में कन्नड़ बोल और गीत से पत्थर पर उतरा, और वही कदम आज लिखे हर शब्द को आकार देता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a quiet village stone carried the first firm breath of written Kannada
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक शांत गाँव का पत्थर बना लिखित कन्नड़ की पहली ठोस साँस
